explanation:
> Theorem 2.5. (Belyi Maps Noncritical at Prescribed Points) Let X be a smooth, proper, connected curve over \overline{\mathbb{Q}} and S,T \subseteq X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) finite sets of \overline{\mathbb{Q}}-rational points such that S \cap T = \emptyset. Then there exists a morphism \phi : X \to \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} such that: (a) \phi is unramified over \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\backslash\{0,1,\infty\}; (b) \phi(S) \subseteq \{0,1,\infty\}; (c) we have \phi(T) \cap \{0,1,\infty\} = \emptyset. Moreover, if X, S, and T are defined over a number field F, then \phi may be taken to be defined over F.

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Theorem 2.5, printed pp. 5–6.

Let N∈ℕ and M:Model N. Its field K=M.K is an intermediate field of the algebraic closure of ℚ(t), with u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, and K is finite-dimensional of degree N over ℚ(u). A place P is any proper valuation subring O_P of K containing ℚ; κ(P) is its full residue field and res_P:O_P→κ(P) its actual residue homomorphism. Fix the algebraic closure ℚ̄ of ℚ. An algebraic point x=(P,σ) includes any such place and any ring embedding σ:κ(P)→ℚ̄ of the full residue field. For f∈O_P, x.eval(f)=σ(res_P(f)). All such places and embeddings are quantified over. The explicit hypothesis hDVR:PlacesDiscrete M says every O_P is a discrete valuation ring. The model also supplies IsCurveField K, from which the normalized integer order ord_P=P.ord is obtained; its defined value at 0 is ord_P(0)=0. The model order defined using hDVR agrees with P.ord. Write e_P(f)=ramIdx M hDVR f P∈ℤ. For f∈O_P this is ord_P(q(f)), with q the minimal polynomial over ℚ of res_P(f); for f∉O_P it is −ord_P(f). The model-derived curve-field structure makes κ(P) finite-dimensional over ℚ. The projective value z_x(f)=noncriticalValue M x f is σ(res_P(f)) when f∈O_P and ∞ otherwise; Pt=Option ℚ̄ records finite values as some z and ∞ as none. For a rational polynomial p of positive natural degree, its projective map sends finite z to p(z) and ∞ to ∞. The natural-number elementary polynomial index is natDegree(p) at ∞ and the root multiplicity of z in p̄(X)−p(z) at finite z, where p̄ is obtained by mapping every rational coefficient into ℚ̄. For transcendental φ, every point x, and positive-degree rational p, the value of p(φ) is the polynomial Pt image of φ’s value. Its actual index is the index of φ times the elementary polynomial index at that value. In symbols, z_x(p(φ))=p(z_x(φ)) on the projective line and e_P(p(φ))=e_P(φ)·(e_p(z_x(φ)):ℤ), with P=x.P. The natural elementary index is cast to ℤ. There is no output-transcendence conjunct in this particular statement. The written proof uses the OPEN regular-point and pole polynomial-order children, so it remains dependent on those obligations.
